The company originated as a division of [[Carlson Companies]], which owned [[Radisson Hotels]], [[Country Inns & Suites]] and other brands. In 1994, Carlson signed a franchise agreement with [[SAS International Hotels]] (SIH), after which SIH started to use the brand [[Radisson SAS]] in the Europe, Middle East and Africa markets. In 2005, Carlson acquired 25% of the shares of SIH, at that time known as [[Rezidor SAS Hospitality]]. In 2010, [[Rezidor Hotel Group]] (formerly Rezidor SAS) became a subsidiary of Carlson. The enlarged hotel group adopted a new trading name, Carlson Rezidor Hotel Group, which was one of the top hotel corporations in 2013.{{cite book | editor-last=Ivanova | editor-first=Maya | editor-last2=Ivanov | editor-first2=Stanislav | editor-last3=Magnini | editor-first3=Vincent P. | title=The Routledge Handbook of Hotel Chain Management | publisher=Routledge (Taylor & Francis Group) | year=2016 | isbn=9781315752532 | url=https://www.routledge.com/The-Routledge-Handbook-of-Hotel-Chain-Management/Ivanova-Ivanov-Magnini/p/book/9781138805057|chapter=Hotel chains, globalisation, and politics|first=Craig|last=Webster}} In 2016, Carlson Companies sold Carlson Rezidor Hotel Group to Chinese conglomerate [[HNA Group]]. In the fourth quarter of 2017, Carlson Hotels, Inc. (the [[holding company]] of the hotel group) was renamed Radisson Hospitality, Inc., while the listed subsidiary (Rezidor Hotel Group AB) was renamed Radisson Hospitality AB. In 2018, HNA Group re-sold Radisson to a consortium led by a multi-national hospitality company, [[Jinjiang International|Jin Jiang International]]. As of 2021, Radisson Hotel Group owns or operates nine hotel brands: Radisson Collection, [[Radisson Blu]], [[Radisson Hotels|Radisson]], [[Radisson Red]], Radisson Individuals, [[Park Plaza Hotels & Resorts|Park Plaza]], [[Park Inn by Radisson]], Country Inn & Suites by Radisson and prizeotel. The loyalty program is known as Radisson Rewards. In June 2022, Radisson Hotel Group agreed to sell Radisson Hotels Americas (consisting of the Radisson franchise agreements, operations and intellectual property in the United States, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean) to [[Choice Hotels]] for $675 million.{{Cite web |title=Choice Hotels International to Acquire Radisson Hotel Group Americas |url=http://media.choicehotels.com/2022-06-13-Choice-Hotels-International-to-Acquire-Radisson-Hotel-Group-Americas |access-date=2022-06-13 |website=Choice Hotels International - Media Center |language=en}} The deal closed on August 11, 2022.{{cite web | url=http://media.choicehotels.com/2022-08-11-Choice-Hotels-International-Completes-Acquisition-of-Radisson-Hotels-Americas | title=Choice Hotels International Completes Acquisition of Radisson Hotels Americas }} ==History== ===Predecessors=== {{see also|Carlson (company)|Rezidor Hotel Group|Radisson Hotels}} [[Curt Carlson]], founder of [[Carlson (company)|the namesake company]], bought Radisson Hotel in downtown Minneapolis in 1962{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-feb-22-mn-10529-story.html|title=Curtis Carlson; Owner of Radisson Hotels|date=February 22, 1999|access-date=January 18, 2019|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|type=obituary}}{{cite journal|title=Carlson Companies, Inc.|journal=International Directory of Company Histories|volume=181|date=2016|orig-year=previous versions of the article were published in vol.6, 22 and 87|publisher=St. James Press ([[Gale (publisher)|Gale]], [[Cengage Learning]] group)|location=Farmington Hills, Michigan|first1=Elisabeth|last1=Rourke|first2=David E.|last2=Salamie|first3=Kathleen|last3=Peippo|first4=Carrie|last4=Rothburd|isbn=978-1-55862-955-4|editor-first=Jay P.|editor-last=Pederson}}{{rp|90}} (Radisson Hotel Group claimed it was 1960).{{cite web|url=https://www.radissonhotelgroup.com/history-heritage|title=History & Heritage|date=c. 2018|access-date=January 20, 2019|publisher=Radisson Hotel Group}} 40 years later, the hotel division of Carlson had expanded into one of the top hotel corporations, as of 2013. On top of [[Radisson Hotels]], the division also owned several other brands, such as [[Park Inn by Radisson|Park Inn]], [[Park Plaza Hotels & Resorts|Park Plaza]] (acquired in 2000), Country Inns & Suites (founded by Carlson in 1986), etc. The division acquired the brand [[Regent Hotels & Resorts|Regent]] in 1997, but sold the brand in 2010. In 1994, the division expanded into [[Europe, the Middle East and Africa]] markets (EMEA) by signing a franchise agreement with [[SAS Group]]'s [[SAS International Hotels]] (SIH). SIH would use Carlson's brand Radisson in EMEA.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/08/12/business/company-news-radisson-and-sas-form-hotel-pact.html|title=Radisson and SAS Form Hotel Pact|date=August 12, 1994|access-date=January 17, 2019|orig-year=digitalized on n.d.|newspaper=The New York Times|first=Edwin|last=McDowell}} The agreement gave birth of the co-brand [[Radisson SAS]], which became [[Radisson Blu]] since 2009. SAS International Hotels, later known as Rezidor SAS Hospitality in 2001 and then Rezidor Hotel Group in 2006, had expanded into a hotel group that consisted of more than 320 hotels as of 2008.{{cite news|url=https://www.ft.com/content/9f3ee922-f97a-11dc-9b7c-000077b07658|title= Kurt Ritter: Tricks of a half-century in hospitality |date=March 27, 2008|access-date=January 17, 2019|newspaper=Financial Times|location=London|first=Roger|last=Blitz|type=news report and interview|url-access=limited}} The franchise agreement was renewed in 2002 and again in 2005. The 2002 deal added Park Inn, Regent and Country Inns into the agreement, while in 2005 agreement, Carlson purchased 25% shares of Rezidor SAS from SAS Group. The 2005 franchise agreement would last until year 2052.{{Cite web |title=Rezidor SAS Hospitality And Carlson Hotels Worldwide Complete Strategic Agreement |url=https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4023756.html |access-date=2023-01-10 |website=Hospitality Net |language=en-us}} Rezidor Hotel Group also had other brands, such as Hotel Missoni, which was licensed from [[Missoni]]. ===Carlson Rezidor Hotel Group=== [[File:Carlson rezidor hotel group logo.jpg|thumb|150px|Logo of Carlson Rezidor Hotel Group]] Rezidor Hotel Group, formerly Rezidor SAS, became a listed company in 2006.{{rp|380}}{{cite press release|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20061128005480/en/OMX-Rezidor-Hotel-Group-Listed-Nordic-Exchange|title= OMX: Rezidor Hotel Group Listed on the Nordic Exchange |date=November 28, 2006|access-date=January 17, 2019|publisher=OMX; Rezidor Hotel Group|agency=Business Wire|location=Sweden}}{{cite press release|url=https://www.sasgroup.net/en/sas-group-announces-publication-of-prospectus-ipo-timetable-and-price-range-for-the-listing-of-rezidor-hotel-group-ab-publ-2/|title=SAS Group Announces publication of Prospectus, IPO Timetable and Price Range for the Listing of Rezidor Hotel Group AB (publ)|date=November 13, 2006|access-date=January 17, 2019|publisher=SAS Group}} SAS Group ceased to be the shareholder of Rezidor Hotel Group in 2007,{{cite journal|title=Rezidor Hotel Group AB|date=2010|volume=118|editor-first=Jay P.|editor-last=Pederson|journal=International Directory of Company History|publisher=St. James Press ([[Gale (publisher)|Gale]], [[Cengage Learning]] group)|first=M. Radisson Hospitality Belgium SRL/BV, trading as Radisson Hotel Group is an international hospitality company headquartered in Brussels, Belgium. 
The company originated as a division of Carlson Companies, which owned Radisson Hotels, Country Inns & Suites and other brands. In 1994, Carlson signed a franchise agreement with SAS International Hotels (SIH), after which SIH started to use the brand Radisson SAS in the Europe, Middle East and Africa markets. In 2005, Carlson acquired 25% of the shares of SIH, at that time known as Rezidor SAS Hospitality. In 2010, Rezidor Hotel Group (formerly Rezidor SAS) became a subsidiary of Carlson. The enlarged hotel group adopted a new trading name, Carlson Rezidor Hotel Group, which was one of the top hotel corporations in 2013.
In 2016, Carlson Companies sold Carlson Rezidor Hotel Group to Chinese conglomerate HNA Group. In the fourth quarter of 2017, Carlson Hotels, Inc. (the holding company of the hotel group) was renamed Radisson Hospitality, Inc., while the listed subsidiary (Rezidor Hotel Group AB) was renamed Radisson Hospitality AB. In 2018, HNA Group re-sold Radisson to a consortium led by a multi-national hospitality company, Jin Jiang International.
As of 2021, Radisson Hotel Group owns or operates nine hotel brands: Radisson Collection, Radisson Blu, Radisson, Radisson Red, Radisson Individuals, Park Plaza, Park Inn by Radisson, Country Inn & Suites by Radisson and prizeotel. The loyalty program is known as Radisson Rewards.
In June 2022, Radisson Hotel Group agreed to sell Radisson Hotels Americas (consisting of the Radisson franchise agreements, operations and intellectual property in the United States, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean) to Choice Hotels for $675 million. The deal closed on August 11, 2022.
